chapter: Teaching, the 1951 Big Show and New York nights
title: Teaching studio; Kenny Burrell as informal student
summary: Students travel from Boston, Montana and San Francisco to study with Collins, who notes Burrell informally learned voicings from him.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Yes, yes. Dick Hyde. Don Rader, Bobby Shuf, let's see, who else. Oh, it was just a great band, it was just a fun band. So as I say I got quite a bit of exposure after that. Then I got the yen to teach again, so I got this studio and I've been teaching two days a week every -- ever since. Now, my students will come -- I just had a student last week to come from Boston to study with me. I had a student to come from Montana, to study with me. I have students come from San Francisco to study with me. You know. So they are advanced students.
Now, this is gratifying, you know. So I'm beginning to write a few things for guitar now.
you said Kenny Burrell was one
Yeah. Well, not formally, but of you know we --

Well yes. He didn't -- wasn't a regular student, you know, but as I say I enjoy doing this, you know. As you know I'm very hung up on chordal structure and progressions, and different voicings, and when I hear someone play I'm on pins and needles because so much they leave out. And I'll give you an example. We were at a party, Kenny and I, and Kenny played a tune for me and he played a very -- beautifully. But there were so many ways he could have gone that he left out and he asked me play it for him, you know, after he had played it. And I really didn't want to -- I wanted to but I didn't want to.

But any way I sat down and I played it for him just to show him how many ways to go, and the different voicing. But this is because I'm just -- this has just been my thing. You know. So now I'm beginning to write a few things for guitar, and just to show, you know, show them how to voice. And different progressions and directions to take.
